messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Wiener Drift Diffusion Model - specifying a parameter with multiple bounds
parts:
I think this is the same question, but you need to do
the transform and apply the Jacobian adjustment.

parameters {
vector[N] tau_raw;

transformed parameters {
vector[N] tau = inv_logit(tau_raw) .* y; // this could also be a local variable

The Jacobian is just

inv_logit(tau_raw[n]) * (1 - inv_logit(tau_raw[n]) * y[n];

and you want it on the log scale, so that's

log_inv_logit(tau_raw[n]) + log1m_inv_logit(tau_raw[n]) + log(y[n])

putting it all together, that should just be:

model {
target += log_inv_logit(tau_raw);
target += log1m_inv_logit(tau_raw);
target += log(y);

It's more efficient to increment in three pieces, but you can put it
all together if you want --- it's not that much less efficient.

And you can drop the y if that's a constant obviously.

I need to put this in the manual, too:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2265#issuecomment-297120950

- Bob

> On Apr 24, 2017, at 1:25 PM, Tiago Cabaço <tiago.jo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> Hello everyone,
>
> I am currently working on a hierarchical version of the wiener diffusion model and I am having some issues with the non-decision time parameter. Since I am trying to estimate one parameter per trial, the estimated non-decision time parameter can't be higher then the actual response time for that trial. If bounds are not specified in the model, rstan won't start sampling.
>
> However, since different trials have different response times, I would like to know if there is a way in which I could parameterize the model so that the upper bound for trial "n" is either given by a function
>
> data{
> int N; // number of trials
> y[N]; //Reaction times
> ...
> }
>
> parameters{
> for (i in 1:N){
> vector<lower=0.0001, upper = y[n] - .01>[N] tau; //non-decision time for trial n
> }
> ...
> }
>
> or by a value from a vector?
>
> data{
> int N; // number of trials
> real y[N]; //Reaction times
> int upper_limit; //upper_limit = y[n] - 0.01
> ...
> }
>
> parameters{
> for (i in 1:N){
> vector<lower=0.0001, upper = upper_lim[n]>[N] tau; //non-decision time for trial n
> }
> ...
> }
>
> Thank you,
>
> Tiago
